Abhaykumar: The son of King Shrenik; known for his immense wisdom and devotion to Bhagawän Mahävir.
Achaurya: Non-stealing; one of the five main vows (also known as Asteya).
Adatädäna: The act of taking something that is not given; stealing.
Adharmästikäy: The medium of rest; the universal substance that helps souls and matter to stay still.
Aghäti Karma: Non-destructive karmas that determine the physical conditions of the soul's current life.
Ahimsä: Non-violence; the fundamental Jain vow of not causing harm to any living being in any form.
Aimutta Muni: A famous child-monk known for his innocent wisdom and sudden enlightenment.
Ajiva: Non-living substances; the five substances in the universe that lack consciousness.
Äkäshästikäy: Space; the universal substance that provides accommodation to all other substances.
Alokäkäsh: The empty space beyond the universe (Loka) where only space exists.
Anand Shravak: A prominent lay disciple of Bhagawän Mahävir known for his strict adherence to vows.
Ananthat: Infinite; the inherent, unlimited qualities of a liberated soul.
Anekäntaväd: The doctrine of many-sidedness; the principle that truth has many perspectives.
Antaräya Karma: Obstructive karma that creates hurdles in performing good deeds or gaining benefits.
Anuvrat: The five small or partial vows observed by Jain laypeople (Shrävaks).
Aparigraha: Non-possessiveness or non-attachment to worldly belongings and internal passions.
Apkäy: Water-bodied living beings; one-sensed souls that have water as their body.
Arihant: A soul who has conquered all inner enemies and attained omniscience while still in a body.
Äsrav: The influx of karmic matter into the soul.
Ästikäy: A substance that occupies more than one space-point (Pradesh).
Ävashyak: The six essential daily spiritual duties for Jains to purify the soul.
Äyushya Karma: The karma that determines the specific life span of a living being.
Bandh: The bondage of karma; the process of karmic particles sticking to the soul.
Bhagawän: The Supreme Being; a term used for Tirthankars and liberated souls.
Bhävanä: Reflections or mental contemplations used to cultivate spiritual purity.
Brahmacharya: Chastity or celibacy; one of the five main vows.
Chandanbälä: The first female disciple (Sädhvi) and head of the female order under Bhagawän Mahävir.
Darshan: Perception or vision; the general awareness that precedes detailed knowledge.
Darshanävarniya Karma: Karma that obscures the soul's inherent power of perception.
Das Lakshan: The ten-day festival celebrated by Digambars to honor ten supreme virtues.
Dharma: Religion; the true nature of a substance; also the universal medium of motion.
Dharmästikäy: The medium of motion; the substance that helps souls and matter move.
Digambar: One of the two main Jain sects; monks of this sect do not wear clothes.
Ghäti Karma: Destructive karmas that obscure the true, infinite qualities of the soul.
Gotra Karma: Karma that determines one's status, family, and surroundings.
Gunasthän: The fourteen stages of spiritual evolution a soul passes through to reach liberation.
Gupti: Restraint of mind, speech, or body to prevent the influx of karma.
Himsä: Violence; causing harm to any living being.
Indriya: Senses; the five physical tools (touch, taste, smell, sight, hearing) used to perceive the world.
Jiva: The living being or soul; characterized by consciousness (Upayog).
Jnän: Knowledge; the soul's ability to know the details and characteristics of objects.
Jnänävarniya Karma: Karma that obscures the soul's inherent power of infinite knowledge.
Käl: Time; the substance responsible for the continuous change in all other substances.
Karma: Minute particles of matter that attach to the soul due to its activities and passions.
Kashäy: Internal passions (Anger, Pride, Deceit, Greed) that cause karmic bondage.
Leshyä: The state of mind or 'coloration' of the soul reflecting its current passions.
Lokäkäsh: The occupied universe where all six universal substances (Dravyas) exist.
Mahävrat: The five great vows taken by Jain monks and nuns for absolute restraint.
Mohaniya Karma: The deluding karma that obscures right belief and conduct; the most difficult karma to overcome.
Moksh: Total liberation; the state where the soul is permanently free from all karma.
Näm Karma: Karma that determines the physical body, its shape, and individual characteristics.
Nav Tattva: The nine fundamentals that explain the soul's relationship with the universe and karma.
Nirjarä: The partial shedding or eradication of accumulated karmas from the soul.
Panch Parameshthi: The five supreme beings worshipped in the Navkär Mantra.
Paryushan: The most significant annual festival for Shvetämbars, focused on repentance and fasting.
Prän: Life-forces or vitalities that sustain a worldly soul; humans have ten Präns.
Prithvikäy: Earth-bodied living beings; one-sensed souls that have earth as their body.
Pudgala: Matter; the only substance that has color, taste, smell, and touch.
Punya: Wholesome or virtuous karma that results in worldly happiness.
Ratna Trayi: The Three Jewels of Jainism: Right Belief, Right Knowledge, and Right Conduct.
Sädhäran Jiva: Common-bodied plants where many souls share a single body (e.g., root vegetables).
Sämäyika: A ritual of equanimity practiced for 48 minutes to achieve mental peace.
Samsäri: A worldly soul currently caught in the cycle of birth and death.
Samvar: The process of stopping the influx of new karma into the soul.
Satya: Truthfulness; one of the five main vows.
Shad Dravya: The six universal substances that make up the entire universe.
Shravak: A Jain layman who follows the minor vows (Anuvrats).
Shravika: A Jain laywoman who follows the minor vows (Anuvrats).
Shvetämbar: One of the two main Jain sects; monks and nuns of this sect wear white clothes.
Siddha: A fully liberated soul who has shed all eight karmas and resides in Siddha-shilä.
Sthävar Jiva: Immobile beings with only one sense (the sense of touch).
Tap: Austerity or penance; external or internal practices used to shed karma.
Tejukäy: Fire-bodied living beings; one-sensed souls that have fire as their body.
Tirthankar: One of the 24 supreme teachers who re-establish the Jain order in every half-cycle.
Trasa Jiva: Mobile beings with two, three, four, or five senses.
Upayog: Consciousness; the defining characteristic of the soul, consisting of knowledge and perception.
Vardhamän: The childhood name of Bhagawän Mahävir, meaning 'ever-increasing'.
Väyukäy: Air-bodied living beings; one-sensed souls that have air as their body.
Vedaniya Karma: Karma that determines the experience of worldly pleasure or pain.
